what_its_for: Almotriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults and teenagers (12 years and older). It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is NOT used to prevent migraines or to treat other types of headaches.
how_to_take: Take almotriptan by mouth as a tablet as soon as you feel a migraine coming on. You can take it with or without food. If your headache comes back after getting better, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets in any 24-hour period. If your first dose does not help at all, do not take a second dose for that same migraine — call your doctor instead.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 6.25 mg or 12.5 mg taken as a single tablet at the start of a migraine. Your doctor will decide which dose is right for you. If needed, a second dose may be taken 2 hours after the first, but no more than 2 doses (25 mg total) in one day. For teenagers aged 12–17, the usual dose is 6.25 mg to 12.5 mg. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: Almotriptan is not taken on a regular daily schedule — it is only taken when you have a migraine. There is no 'missed dose' to worry about. Simply take it when a migraine starts, following your doctor's instructions.
storage: Store almotriptan at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Store it in a dry place, away from bathrooms. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking almotriptan within 24 hours of using another triptan medication (such as sumatriptan or rizatriptan) or ergotamine-type medicines (such as Cafergot or Migranal). Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if this medication makes you feel drowsy or dizzy. Limit alcohol use, as it can worsen migraines and side effects. Do not overuse this medication — using migraine treatments more than 10 days per month can cause 'medication overuse headache.'
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; shortness of breath; sudden severe headache different from your usual migraine; weakness or numbness on one side of your body; slurred speech; vision changes; fast or irregular heartbeat; severe stomach pain; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your headache does not improve, if you need to take this medicine more than 10 days per month, or if your migraines are getting worse.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel relief within 30 minutes to 2 hours after taking almotriptan. It works best when taken at the first sign of a migraine. It may not work as well if you wait until the headache is severe.
special_populations: Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose (6.25 mg) and limit you to no more than 1 dose per day if you have kidney or liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or if you smoke, as this medicine may not be right for you. Older adults (65+): Use with caution; your doctor will guide you. Children under 12: This medication is not approved for children under 12 years old.
